This appeal having been heard and reserved for order, coming on for
pronouncement this day, the court passed the following:
 Judgment

This criminal appeal has been preferred against the judgment passed by Additional Sessions Judge,
Panna on 31.10.1998 in S.T. No.104/1996.

By the impugned judgment the appellants were convicted under Section 498-A of IPC and were sentenced to undergo three years R.I. and fine of Rs.2,000/-
with default stipulation.

sentences.text: During pendency of this appeal, it was reported that appellant no.2 has died.
No one appeared on her behalf to request that the appeal be continued, therefore, this appeal stands abated so far as appellant no.2 is concerned.
3. The brief facts of prosecution story are that deceased Janki Bai got married about six years prior to the incident to a man of village Teer.
She was abandoned by her husband for the reason that she failed to bear any child.
About three years prior to the incident deceased Janki Bai was given in conjugal relationship to appellant no.1 Leeladhar, who was having illicit relationship with appellant No.2 Sundar Bai.
They both used to threaten Janki Bai by asking her not to raise any objection to their relationship.
Appellant No.2 Sundar Bai used to come to the house of Leeladhar and live there.
Janki Bai was sharing facts about this illicit relationship with her relatives and also the harassment that was being caused to her by both these persons.
On the date of incident she put herself on fire.
She was taken by Leeladhar, Sundar Bai and other persons to Shahnagar Hospital (Panna) from where she was referred to Community Hospital Katni.
A constable Lakhan was taking her to that hospital, but on the way she died.
The merg was registered and the enquiry was conducted.
On this basis, an FIR was registered under Section 306/34 against appellants Leeladhar and Sundar Bai.
After investigation, they were charge-sheeted and put to trial.

Under the impugned judgment they acquitted of the charge of Sections 302/34 and also of alternative charge of Section 306 of IPC, but were convicted under Section 498-A of IPC and sentenced as mentioned above.
4. In this criminal appeal, the grounds raised are that the learned trial Judge erred in convicting the appellant.
The dying declaration of Janki Bai was totally ignored in which she had informed about the accident.
Parents of Janki Bai have failed to report any complaint against appellant despite claiming that they were aware of illicit relationship of appellant no.1.
Even after the death of Janki Bai on 01.10.1996 they did not report the matter until 06.10.1996.
The cousin of Janki Bai stated that he had seen the appellant No.1 and Janki Bai living happily, but this evidence was totally ignored.
It is, therefore, prayed that the impugned judgment be set aside and appellant Leeladhar be acquitted of the charge.

5. The State has opposed the present appeal claiming that the judgment of conviction and sentence,
which has been passed by the learned trial Court is based on well considered facts and does not warrant any interference.

6. The learned counsel for appellant has addressed during final arguments this important aspect of conviction that appellant no.2 Sundar Bai (since dead) was not a relative of appellant no.1 while only the relatives of husband can be punished under Section 498-A of IPC.
He has drawn the attention of this Court that learned trial Court has failed to appreciate this important fact and has wrongly convicted appellant no.2 Sundar Bai.

7. Extending this argument to appellant no.1 Leeladhar as well, this Court finds that in the entire prosecution evidence not a single fact was stated regarding the marriage between Leeladhar and Jankibai.

Ramsahay (PW/2), the father of Janki Bai disclosed on oath that Janki Bai was married to another person, who abandoned her and then Janki Bai was given in conjugal relationship to appellant no.1 Leeladhar.

The statement of this witness makes no reference to the marriage Leeladhar & Ors. vs The State Of M.P. on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91379383/
2 solemnized between Janki Bai and Leeladhar.

sentences.text: Similar is the statement of Seetabai (PW/3), the mother of Janki Bai.
Rajju (PW/4) is the relative of Janki Bai, but his statements have also failed to disclose the fact of her marriage to Leeladhar.
Ramnath (PW/5), Mansingh (PW/6), Arun Kumar (PW/7) and Prem Singh (PW/8) also do not testify that there was a marriage solemnized between Leeladhar and Janki Bai.
The statements of Arun Kumar (PW/7) and Premsingh (PW/8) further clarify that Janki Bai was brought by appellant Leeladhar from somewhere near Chhatarpur about 3-4 years prior to her death.
8. It is evident that not a single prosecution witness including close relatives of Janki Bai could prove that Janki Bai was the legally wedded wife of appellant Leeladhar.
Without there being any solemnization of marriage, appellant Leeladhar cannot be considered as the husband of deceased Janki Bai.
The impugned judgment is examined in this perspective and it is evident that the trial Court has nowhere considered the marital relationship between the deceased and appellant Leeladhar.

Without considering this important aspect the offence under Section 498-A of IPC was found to be established and this legal aspect was completely ignored that the offence of Section 498- A of IPC is attracted only to marital relationship, nothing less.
Thus, the conviction under Section 498-A of IPC is clearly erroneous.

9. The decision of Hon'ble the Supreme Court rendered in Shivcharan Lal Verma & another Vs. State of M.P., 2002 2 Crimes (SC) 177 is pertinent to be referred here wherein a three Judge Bench of Apex Court held that for a prosecution under Section 498A of IPC, there must be a valid marital relationship between the accused and the victim.

entities.text: Shivcharan Lal Verma & another Vs. State of M.P., 2002 2 Crimes (SC) 177
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the present case, there is not only want of evidence on the point of solemnization of marriage between the deceased and appellant-Leeladhar,
but this fact has also gone unchallenged that deceased was earlier married to another person and without the dissolution of that wedlock, deceased was living in marital relationship with the present appellant.
Therefore, in the absence of dissolution of first marriage of deceased, she cannot be considered as a legally wedded wife of appellant.

Though there have been some later decisions of Hon'ble the Supreme Court rendered in Reema Agrawal Vs. Anupam, AIR 2004 Supreme Court 1418 and K. Subbharao Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, AIR 2009 Supreme Court 2684 where liberal interpretation was given to the term "husband", but the earlier decision of Larger Bench in the case of Shivcharan Lal (supra) was not considered in these smaller Bench judgments.

entities.text: Reema Agrawal Vs. Anupam, AIR 2004 Supreme Court 1418
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: K. Subbharao Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, AIR 2009 Supreme Court 2684
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, this leads to the legal interpretation that Section 498A of IPC has applicability only on valid marital relationship.

10. On the basis of foregoing discussions, this Court considers that the finding to hold appellant no.1-Leeladhar guilty of causing harassment to deceased Janki Bai was incorrect as she was not his legally wedded wife.
Therefore, his conviction under Section 498-A of IPC being improper is set aside.
He was acquitted by the trial Court itself, for the offence of Section 302/34 and 306 of IPC.
Further there are no allegations proved in the case against appellant which would make him liable to an offence of lesser gravity.
11. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The conviction and sentence of appellant no.1 Leeladhar is set aside.
The appellant is in jail.
He be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
The fine amount, if any, deposited by him shall be refunded to him.
